title: Thomason comparison for lax and oplax Grothendieck constructions
statement:
Use the simplicial replacements $\mathrm{BK},\mathrm{KB}$ of [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus] and weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For a small category $C$ and a diagram $F:C\to\mathrm{Cat}$ of small categories define two categories $\operatorname{Th}_C F$ and $\operatorname{Gr}_C F$, both with objects $(c,z)$, $z\in F(c)$. In $\operatorname{Th}_C F$ a morphism $(c,z)\to(c',z')$ is a pair $a:c\to c'$, $b:F(a)z\to z'$. In $\operatorname{Gr}_C F$ it is a pair $a:c'\to c$, $b:z\to F(a)z'$. Identities and composition use the corresponding functors $F(a)$ and composition in the fibers. Write $NE$ for the nerve of a category $E$, whose $r$-simplices are strings of $r$ composable arrows, with composition/deletion faces and identity-insertion degeneracies. There are natural weak homotopy equivalences
$$\mathrm{BK}_C(NF)\longrightarrow N\operatorname{Th}_C F,\qquad
\mathrm{KB}_C(NF)\longrightarrow N\operatorname{Gr}_C F.$$
They are natural under natural transformations of diagrams and reindexing functors and send a degree-zero pair $(c,z)$ to that same object. In particular, if $F\to G$ is a natural transformation such that every $NF(c)\to NG(c)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, the induced functors $\operatorname{Th}_C F\to\operatorname{Th}_C G$ and $\operatorname{Gr}_C F\to\operatorname{Gr}_C G$ induce weak homotopy equivalences on nerves.
